evidence: src/application/TaskDTO.ts declares `interface TaskDTO` with `dueDate: string | null`, but no use case returns or accepts TaskDTO.
src/application/AddTaskUseCase.ts: `execute(...): Task` takes `dueDate: Date | null` and returns the domain `Task`, not TaskDTO.
src/application/CreateProjectUseCase.ts: `execute(id, name): Project` returns the domain entity, while src/application/ProjectDTO.ts declares an unused `ProjectDTO`.
src/application/CreateUserUseCase.ts: `execute(id, name): User` returns the domain entity, while src/application/UserDTO.ts declares an unused `UserDTO`.
src/application/ListTasksUseCase.ts: `execute(...): Task[]` and src/application/MarkTaskDoneUseCase.ts / AssignTaskUseCase.ts: `execute(...): Task` all expose domain entities across the boundary.

src/application/AssignTaskUseCase.ts and src/application/MarkTaskDoneUseCase.ts both contain `const task = this.taskRepository.getById(taskId); if (!task) throw new Error(`Task with id ${taskId} not found`)`.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module covers one concern: use cases for task, project and user management. But its boundary abstraction is used inconsistently. It declares output DTOs (ProjectDTO, TaskDTO, UserDTO), yet every use case returns a domain entity instead (Task, Project, User). None of the module's files use the DTOs. So the boundary exposes domain entities, and the mapping from entity to DTO (including turning dueDate from a Date into a string) has to happen outside the module, probably once per controller. That bypasses the module's own boundary abstraction. A smaller issue: the 'Task with id ... not found' load-and-guard is written out in both AssignTaskUseCase and MarkTaskDoneUseCase rather than kept in one place. Domain invariants are delegated properly (canMarkDone, withStatus and withAssignee live on Task).

violations.message: TaskDTO is declared as the module's boundary type but no use case uses it. Task use cases return the domain Task, so the conversion from Task to TaskDTO (including turning dueDate from Date to string) has to happen outside the module.
ProjectDTO is declared but unused. CreateProjectUseCase returns the domain Project instead, so the module's boundary abstraction is bypassed.
UserDTO is declared but unused. CreateUserUseCase returns the domain User instead, so the module's boundary abstraction is bypassed.
execute returns the domain Task rather than the module's TaskDTO, which leaks a domain entity across the application boundary that the module itself defines.
